meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have forty minutes before a call, and I'd like to know why my son's grade changed on his phone in the middle of class.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Procedure 4.1 says you speak with Owen first, and 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in. You've admitted the second. Did you do the first?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Turn the screen, I'm searching the scene now. A student who gets a line wrong has gotten a line wrong, so what ties that to anything else?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4. I want it in writing tonight, with nothing on his record, and no classmates anywhere near that room. You still haven't answered me on 4.1.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You admitted entering the zero before you called me and offered a supervised rewrite under 4.4 on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal, but nothing was agreed. I still require written confirmation that the rewrite is private, that its mark replaces the zero, that nothing goes on Owen's record, and an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen under 4.1 before the zero went in. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback, with the 4.4 rewrite offered but not accepted; she still wants it in writing, private, with nothing on his record and an answer on 4.1, and if you give her all of that, it is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence and moved on, which took away her first grievance and kept her listening.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether Owen was spoken to first unanswered, so her strongest procedural point stayed open the whole meeting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with the 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58 edits came close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what ties a wrong line to anything else, answer that before moving to the rewrite, so the evidence stands on its own instead of being skipped past.
